messages:
sec-oncall: Deploy bot alerted: base-image signing failed during nightly rebuild - cosign exit 1, KMS DENIED at 02:41 UTC. Putting this thread to coordinate. link: https://ci.internal/rebuilds/4521 :exclamation:

deploy-bot: automatic retry attempted (3/3) and failed, moved to manual queue.

alina: looking... getting `AccessDeniedException` in KMS logs. Could be a key rotation or RBAC change.

benjamin: I rolled a small IAM tweak yesterday to tighten signer role on the kms key for artifact-signer. Did I accidentally drop the service account? pinging ops.

luis: I saw a change from the infra team — they replaced the old key's policy to remove broad binding for `svc-artifact@redwood-infra.iam.gserviceaccount.com`. That was intentional for least-privilege.

jamie: we need the audit trail for the signing attempts. audit-bot, can you surface all KMS grant/deny events + cosign attempts for the last 6 hours?

audit-bot: @jamie attached: KMS audit entries 02:00-03:00 UTC (IDs: kms_evt_987 -> DENY for svc-artifact, kms_evt_988 -> GRANT to build-runner). Cosign logs: cosign:2026-03-21T02:41:01Z -> exit 1, stderr: "rpc error: code = PermissionDenied desc = requestor not authorized".

alina: OK that matches — service account lacked `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeySign` on the key version used.

benjamin: my change removed `member:serviceAccount:svc-artifact@...` from the key binding. I thought build-runner would sign via a delegation/impersonation flow, but CI still uses svc-artifact directly for cosign. My bad.

sec-oncall: Impact assessment — signing failed for 3 images pushed to staging. No production cutovers. No runtime impact, only image attestation missing. Still counts as a compliance gap for our release window.

jamie: action plan: 1) restore minimal signer binding to svc-artifact (benjamin) 2) re-run cosign for the 3 images (alina) 3) verify audit logs and record in incident tracker (sec-oncall) 4) add unit test in CI to catch KMS perms for signer (luis). Can we do that in the next 60 minutes?

benjamin: will restore binding now. Command I run: ```
gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding artifacts-key \
  --location=global --keyring=redwood-keyring \
  --member="serviceAccount:svc-artifact@redwood-infra.iam.gserviceaccount.com" \
  --role="roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeySign"
```

alina: after you, I'll trigger signing: `for img in $(cat failed_images); do cosign sign --key kms://projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/redwood-keyring/cryptoKeys/artifacts-key@$img; done` — will post results.

benjamin: done. IAM binding added. gcloud returned etag update ok.

audit-bot: observed IAM change event iam_evt_5643 by benjamin@redwood at 02:52 UTC.

alina: re-run started. cosign output: image-a: signed ✅, image-b: signed ✅, image-c: signed ✅. All pushed to staging registry with attestations.

sec-oncall: good. Now we need postmortem notes for compliance: timeline, root cause, and remediation. Preliminary root cause: manual RBAC hardening removed service account binding used directly by CI signing job.

luis: remediation items I propose: 1) update infra PR template to require KMS accessor checklist, 2) add CI check that exercises signing path using a test key and fails the PR if signer SA cannot sign, 3) rotate key material on schedule and automate the binding check during rotation.

jamie: also recommend short-term guardrail: add an automated preflight that runs whenever an IAM change touches the artifacts-key or keyring and notifies #eng-release with a summary and required manual approve test.

benjamin: agreed — I'll open the infra PR with the rollback-safe binding change and a note about coordinating with release on key rotations.

alina: I'll create an internal checklist entry in the incident tracker and attach cosign logs + audit events.

sec-oncall: Ownership: benjamin -> infra PR, luis -> CI signing test, alina -> re-run + artifact verification + logs, jamie -> add preflight notifier, sec-oncall -> incident writeup and timeline. Target: docs and tests merged by end of week.

benjamin: one follow-up Q: do we want to move cosign to use short-lived impersonated creds instead of a static service account? That would limit blast radius.

luis: yes, implement impersonation via Workload Identity or token exchange, but that needs changes to runners. We'll spec it as a medium-term task.

sec-oncall: For now, restore binding is fine. Create a short RFC for impersonation pattern; tag security and infra.

jamie: I'll draft the preflight check today. Pseudocode: ```
if iam_change.targets_key(artifacts-key):
  run_sign_test(test_image)
  if fail: block_merge_and_notify()
```

alina: logged incident 2026-03-21-4521 with attachments. Marking severity: S3 (compliance).

deploy-bot: CI build requeued: #4521 -> manual sign done.

sec-oncall: closing this thread — keep updates in the incident doc. If anyone finds related failures in the next 24h, ping this thread. :thumbsup:

benjamin: noted, will follow up with PR link shortly.

luis: will pick up CI test tomorrow morning.

jamie: done drafting notifier, will share in #eng-release for feedback.

alina: thanks all.
